channel.title: Personal AI Agents (Update Bot)
channel.description: Latest features and updates for personal AI agents: Grok Bot, Hermes Agent, Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so dots can shop and check out for you
item.description:
OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on Friday, Nov 13, letting its dots agents help you decide what to buy and complete the purchase in chat. You add an eligible card once; at checkout the Wallet charges it with a payment token, so your actual card details are never shared with the dot or the merchant.

You still review the items, total and card first, and approve each purchase with a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint. It is rolling out first to a limited number of U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers, 18 and up, with a U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard or American Express card.

item.title: Tuya connects Meta's Muse to smart-home devices through cloud APIs
item.description:
Tuya Smart announced on Nov 12 an open-source skill, gadget-tuya-cloud-devices, that lets Meta's Muse query and control devices in a user's Tuya account through cloud APIs, Unite.AI reports. No local device keys, shared network or firmware changes are needed.

Tuya says its platform covers more than 3,000 device categories, though the skill's API endpoints are still trial-phase with rate limits, and its submission to Meta's Muse Gadgets project (PR #61) is still in review.

item.title: CopilotKit releases OpenBot 1.0, a self-hostable agent workspace where each Bot gets its own computer
item.description:
CopilotKit released OpenBot 1.0 on Nov 9, an MIT-licensed, self-hostable agent workspace, MarkTechPost reports. Each Bot gets its own computer — a container with its own Chromium browser, logins and files — and any agent that speaks the AG-UI protocol can plug in.

Personal use is free and runs locally; OpenBot for Business costs up to $29 per active user a month. It supports OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Grok and open models via subscriptions or API keys.

item.title: Meta's Muse can now call US businesses for paid subscribers
item.description:
Meta's Muse can now place phone calls to US businesses on behalf of paid subscribers, TechCrunch reports. Chief AI officer Alexandr Wang announced the rollout on X on Nov 12, after a limited test that began in September.

Muse can handle reservations, scheduling and hold times — the calls people least want to make, like the cable company or the DMV. Calling is paid-only, from $20 a month; Wang also said Muse's dedicated email address will reach free users within the week.

item.title: Grok Bot on Mac can now use Messages, Mail, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Location and Contacts
item.description:
SpaceXAI's Grok Bot on Mac can now work directly with Apple's built-in apps. The official @bot account announced it can use Messages, Mail, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Location and Contacts.

Once you grant access per app, the Bot can read and send messages, search and draft emails, read and write notes, and check reminders, pulling context from your own records instead of relying on prompts alone.

The rollout is gradual, so some users may see only some apps at first. It lands a day after Grok Bot 1.0 left beta on Nov 11.

item.title: Claude will soon join your team meetings and work on tasks live
item.description:
Anthropic announced Claude Meetings: soon you will be able to add Claude to a call to take notes and update the documents your team is working on during the conversation, and start on the tasks being discussed live.

It goes beyond transcription tools that only list action items, because Claude would act on them in the meeting. The feature is planned for Team and Enterprise plans; Anthropic gave no launch date yet, so this is an announcement, not a shipped feature.

item.title: Gopuff launches fully integrated delivery inside Grok Bot
item.description:
Gopuff is the first company to offer a fully integrated delivery experience inside SpaceXAI’s Grok Bot: browse thousands of everyday essentials, build an order, pick a payment method and check out without ever leaving the chat. Orders come from local micro-fulfillment centers and arrive in as fast as 15 minutes.

Connect it from Grok Bot’s Connect Apps button or by saying “Connect to Gopuff”, then ask for a weekly grocery order or a last-minute snack run. Gopuff cites a 99.5% order accuracy rate. It extends the pair’s earlier collaboration on Go, Gopuff’s AI shopping helper.

item.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok Bot 1.0: Team Bots join Slack, Teams and video calls
item.description:
SpaceXAI has launched Grok Bot 1.0, a major update that makes its AI teammates multiplayer: Team Bots can be shared with specific people or groups and brought into Slack, Microsoft Teams and video calls, where they follow discussions and offer to pick up work.

Bots can join Google Meet, Zoom and Microsoft Teams calls from a link, answer in the meeting chat and send a summary afterward. Owners can also share app logins as shared connectors. Meetings are on Team, Enterprise and Ultra plans.

Bots now act more proactively too, spotting unfinished work and following up, with safeguards that respect each person's permissions in shared spaces.

item.title: Meta's Muse now has its own email address: CC it on a thread or forward it a bill
item.description:
Meta's Muse agent now has a dedicated email address that can send and receive email on your behalf. You can add it to an existing thread so it follows the conversation, or forward it a booking, a bill, or a form and ask it to deal with the follow-ups.

Alexandr Wang announced it as “out now to paid subscribers in the US and Canada,” and The Verge reports Meta first showed the feature at Connect in September. Other regions and exact limits weren't announced.

This matters because it changes what you hand the agent: instead of connecting your whole personal mailbox, you can give Muse its own inbox and let vendors write to it directly. It's the same pattern Grok Bot already uses with its own email, and it makes Muse a plausible owner of back-and-forth email chores like chasing bookings, quotes, and bills.

item.title: Grok Bot can now make phone calls, shop with promo codes, and work as a shared Team Bot
item.description:
SpaceXAI's Matt Palmer posted a 7½-minute “What's new in Grok Bot” video on Tuesday, Nov 10, showing the agent doing things it could only talk about before. The headline demo: a Bot calls to cancel an internet plan, waits 14 minutes on hold, identifies itself as a virtual assistant on a recorded line, and turns down a 10%-off retention offer.

Calls work across the US except Washington and Illinois, with a live transcript and a take-over button, and the Bot can work through phone menus. Shopping got the same treatment: product cards now show sale prices, checkout applies promo codes, totals update for shipping and tax before you pay, and checkout cards stay valid for six hours instead of 30 minutes. A new Gift Concierge template tracks holiday gift lists, budgets, and shipping deadlines.

item.title: Meta's Muse India pricing surfaces: ₹1,799 Power, ₹8,999 Maximum (unconfirmed)
item.description:
Meta has yet to officially launch its Muse personal AI agent in India, but its pricing and subscription tiers for the country have surfaced online. The Hindu reports the Power subscription will cost ₹1,799 and the higher-end Maximum plan ₹8,999, roughly in line with the US prices of $20 and $100 a month.

Indian users can currently visit the Muse website to register and join a waitlist for access when the service launches in the country. The report doesn't say whether the quoted prices are monthly or yearly, or what benefits each Indian tier includes — globally, Power offers 500 million Muse tokens a week and Maximum offers 3 billion.

item.title: Hermes Agent v0.23.1 rolls up 618 PRs and fixes plugin installs that silently used a stale catalog
item.description:
Nous Research shipped Hermes Agent v0.23.1 on Nov 9 (about 5:42pm PT), a patch that rolls up roughly 618 merged PRs since v0.23.0 into a stable build for the CLI, installers, the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud.

The headline fix: since Nov 9 the published plugin catalog had grown past the 2 MiB size cap clients accept, so hermes plugins install silently fell back to the bundled catalog, missing new plugins and newer pins. v0.23.1 raises the cap to 16 MiB (PR #151860); older installs keep falling back until they update.

Also in the window but not yet documented: Esc backtrack in the TUI and CLI, group chats that run on a gateway without Desktop and can seat bots from other computers, signing the in-app browser in with your real browser profile and filling saved logins, hermes gateway attach, and new plugin API hooks. Nous says full curated notes come with v0.24.0. Update with hermes update; the .exe/.dmg desktop app is unchanged in this release.

item.title: You can now use a ChatGPT Business plan to power Hermes Agent through Sign in with ChatGPT
item.description:
OpenAI Developers announced on Nov 10 that ChatGPT Business plans now work with Sign in with ChatGPT in outside tools, naming Hermes from Nous Research alongside Notion, v0, Amp, Kilo Code, Warp, OpenClaw and OpenCode.

Nous Research confirmed that the Sign in with ChatGPT flow in Nous Portal now supports Business plans, so a team's ChatGPT Business seat can drive Hermes Agent without a separate API key.

Until now this route was limited to eligible Plus and Pro personal plans, per OpenAI's release notes. Usage counts against the plan's existing allowance.

item.title: Perplexity launches Teammates, always-on personal agents that each work in their own Computer environment
item.description:
Perplexity launched Teammates, personal agents that own ongoing work: they plan projects, run tasks in parallel, remember goals and files across runs, and bring results back for review. It's Perplexity's direct answer to Grok Bot, OpenAI dots and Claude Duet.

Teammates are built on Perplexity Computer. Each one runs in a separate environment with its own browser sessions, saved credentials are encrypted, and you can take over the desktop or redirect a teammate mid-task. They can coordinate other teammates and message coworkers in Slack, per the Nov 6 changelog.

Access is limited to the $200/month Perplexity Max plan on the web, with iOS coming soon, as The Verge notes. The same release added a fully local Computer mode on Apple-silicon Macs.

item.title: Grok Bot can now join your Tailscale tailnets to reach private MCP servers and internal tools
item.description:
The official Grok Bot account announced on Tuesday afternoon that Grok Bot can now join your personal or company tailnets on Tailscale, the private networking service.

That lets your Bot securely reach private MCP servers, internal tools, and apps on your own network without exposing them to the public internet. Tailscale support first showed up in Grok Bot 0.77 prerelease builds in late October, and this is the official rollout.

The Grok Bot changelog doesn't have a matching entry yet, so setup details may land there with the next release notes.

item.title: Grok Bot resets weekly usage limits for every user
item.description:
The official Grok Bot account posted on Nov 9 around 11:17am PT that it has reset weekly limits for all Grok Bot users.

The reset follows a week of complaints on X about tighter Grok Bot usage caps, after Elon Musk said running the agent costs far more than subscriptions bring in.

The post gave no sign that the caps themselves changed, so this looks like a one-time reset rather than a new allowance. The Grok Bot changelog is still on v0.79.3 from Nov 6.

item.title: OpenAI dots can now connect to several of your computers and pick which one runs each task
item.description:
OpenAI Developers announced on Nov 9 that you can now connect multiple local computers to the same dot and choose which one it uses for a task.

OpenAI's example is having the dot build and test your app on a dedicated machine while you keep coding on your laptop. Before this, a dot could link to only one desktop besides its own cloud computer.

You add each machine from the dot's profile in the ChatGPT desktop app, and each task still runs on one computer at a time, according to a summary of the updated docs. There is no extra charge beyond the existing dots plans.

item.title: Meta's Muse agent arrives on Apple Watch and Wear OS
item.description:
Meta launched Muse on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS on Nov 9, which Alexandr Wang announced on X as a "Muse launch alert."

On the watch you can text Muse, dictate to it, or call it, and a watch-face complication opens it in one tap, MacRumors reports. The Apple Watch app ships in version 15.0 of the Muse iOS app.

The Verge also confirmed Wear OS support, while AppleInsider urged readers to skip it over privacy concerns.

item.title: Hermes Cloud agents now open in a browser tab with the full Hermes Desktop interface
item.description:
Nous Research said on Nov 9 that Hermes Cloud agents now open in a browser tab with the same interface as Hermes Desktop.

You launch a personal agent in Nous Portal by picking a name and a model. Nous hosts it 24/7 in its own container, so it can run scheduled jobs and answer you on any channel while your laptop is closed.

Chats, Group Chats, plugins and settings work the same as on your own computer, and you can connect Hermes Desktop to the cloud agent to continue the same chats. Plus, Super and Ultra plans each include one Cloud agent.

item.title: China Telecom's TeleAgent 3.0 gives its agent its own Windows cloud PC
item.description:
China Telecom's AI unit upgraded its TeleAgent super-agent to version 3.0, with the headline change being a dedicated cloud computer for the agent, Science and Technology Daily reported on Nov 9.

Tasks keep running in the cloud even when your own computer is off, and the agent can install software and handle work like Blender 3D modeling, documents and spreadsheets, coding and video editing. You can send tasks from the desktop app, watch progress on your phone, or log in from a web browser.

The release also syncs memory across devices, adds connectors for Chinese office apps like Tencent Meeting and QQ Mail, and isolates the cloud machine from your local device. Hands-on tests by Synced had it install WeCom and build a Blender car model on its own.

item.title: Nous ships an official Security plugin that has Hermes Agent hunt for exploitable bugs in your codebase
item.description:
Nous Research released a new official Security plugin for Hermes Agent on Nov 8, built by @mark_s from his security review experience, Nous announced on X.

Hermes first maps what an attacker could reach and which inputs it trusts, then splits the code across parallel subagents, checks every candidate finding against the code, and traces whether it can actually be exploited.

With test confirmation turned on, Hermes writes a small reproduction for each finding and runs it in a temporary copy of the repo. Each report records the evidence and the findings it ruled out, and exports to SARIF for existing security tools.

You can run it from chat, the CLI, or a new Security page in Hermes Desktop. Cofounder Teknium called it a new official plugin to help analyze codebases for security bugs; it joins the Hermes Marketplace of official plugins.

item.title: OpenAI dots can now use sign-in codes from your connected inbox to log in for you
item.description:
OpenAI's James Sun, who works on browser use for Codex and ChatGPT, announced on Nov 7 that a dot can now use sign-in codes sent to your connected inbox to log in on your behalf.

When a site sends a code, the dot asks first: you can let it use the code once or always allow it to fill codes in. Sun said "lots more sign-in improvements" are coming soon.

OpenAI's dots security FAQ still says you may need to provide a code or take over for some security checks, and ByteForward notes this covers emailed codes, not every sign-in method. Early users quoted by Crypto Briefing report dots sometimes still pause before entering codes.

item.title: Meta launches Muse in Mexico, its first Latin American market, with local shopping and travel connectors
item.description:
Meta has launched Muse in Mexico, the first Latin American country to get its personal AI agent, according to a Nov 5 update to Meta's Latin America newsroom post. People 18 and older can use it in Spanish on iOS, Android, muse.ai, and through WhatsApp.

Muse arrives with local connectors for Cinépolis, Coppel, Despegar, Kavak, Kueski, Liverpool, Rappi and Walmart México, so it can compare prices, track orders, check flights or buy movie tickets from one conversation. WIRED en Español notes some of those brand features will turn on gradually.

Basic use is free, with optional paid plans, matching the US model. Mexico follows Japan (Oct 23) and Singapore (Oct 27) as Muse expands outside the US; Mexico News Daily has an English write-up.

item.title: Meta launches Muse Spaces so you can design custom experiences inside the Muse app
item.description:
Meta today introduced spaces in Muse: custom experiences you create by describing an idea, such as a gift tracker, school dashboard, trip planner, or small-business order tracker.

You can put spaces in the sidebar or main tabs, hide or schedule them, and keep editing with Muse after the first build. Connected apps can keep a space updated in the background.

Spaces are available everywhere Muse is available starting today. Meta says it is also exploring sharing spaces with others.

item.title: Meta rolls Active Memory and Active Focus into Muse via Muse Wonder–trained specialized models
item.description:
Meta is rolling out specialized versions of its Muse and Meta AI models trained with Muse Wonder, bringing Active Memory and Active Focus to everyone on those products (research blog).

Active Memory is meant to keep critical context across conversations; Meta says the new Muse models are 2.4× less likely to forget information needed for goals, with critical-context use rising to 90% from 76% on its eval.

Active Focus is meant to recover from blockers and keep working toward a goal; Meta reports a 67% improvement on everyday Muse tasks when unexpected issues arise. Mark Zuckerberg and AI at Meta also posted the rollout on X.

item.title: Hermes Agent v0.23.0 (Hearth) ships browser Desktop workspace and one gateway for every conversation
item.description:
Nous Research released Hermes Agent v0.23.0 — The Hearth Release on November 5 (about 1:32pm PT), the curated major after the v0.22.1–v0.22.7 patch window (~10,080 commits, ~1,950 merged PRs, 666 contributors since v0.22.0).

Headlines from the release notes:

  • A gateway-hosted Webapp opens the full Desktop workspace in a browser tab (off by default via webapp.enabled / Web Access).
  • One gateway now owns every conversation so CLI, TUI, Desktop, editors, bots, and cron share one session queue and history instead of each running its own agent.
  • Desktop keeps every Hermes machine connected at once; Group Chats get lead/router replies; CLI/TUI draw images inline and support /rewind.
  • Plugins can auto-update; paid MCP tools show price tags and spend limits; the plugin catalog grew from about 600 to over 1,050 entries.

Update with hermes update, the Microsoft Store, or the Docker/Nix images.

item.title: Meta rolls out Muse Realtime Avatar in the US, so you can video-chat with your Muse as a live, animated avatar
item.description:
Meta is rolling out Muse Realtime Avatar in the Muse app in the US starting today, AI at Meta announced on X. The feature, first previewed at Connect, turns Muse Realtime Voice conversations into expressive, interactive avatars with synchronized lip movement, facial expressions and gestures.

According to Meta's research blog, the model streams 448x768 video at 25 frames per second with roughly 870 ms of latency, and generated video carries an invisible Video Seal watermark. Live video chats are for users 18 and older, and there's no developer API.

item.title: OpenAI starts a Nov 4–18 Enterprise dots admin preview; billing for enabled dots begins Nov 18
item.description:
OpenAI's Getting started with your dot help article (updated Nov 4) now says dots are generally available to eligible ChatGPT Enterprise, Edu, and Healthcare workspaces. During an admin preview from November 4 through November 18, 2026, people can use dots if a workspace admin enables access for their role; starting November 18, dots become available by default unless the admin opts out.

For Enterprise pricing, workspaces can pay through flat rates mapped to the type of work or scaled consumption. Dots are free to preview through November 18; billing begins November 18 for all enabled dots. Work a dot delegates to ChatGPT Work or Codex is billed separately at standard rates. Permanent personal-plan dots allowances are still unpublished; extended limits continue "for now."

item.title: Dots iOS app update: inline notification replies, share-to-dot, and Action button shortcuts
item.description:
OpenAI engineer samir (@_samirism) posted on Nov 4 (2:08pm PT) that the latest ChatGPT app release makes dots "significantly faster and more reliable," with iOS changes: reply to your dot inline from a notification, share anything directly to your dot, open your dot from the iPhone Action button, faster loading from notifications, and Gmail links that deeplink to the exact email in the Gmail app.

Dots lead Tibo (@thsottiaux) replied that "Dots just got a massive set of improvements." There was no accompanying help-center or changelog entry.

item.title: Nous opens a 7-day Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon with $20,000 in cash prizes
item.description:
Nous Research launched a Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon on Nov 4 (1:33pm PT), running 7 days with $20,000 in cash prizes plus neon signs, merch, and credits. Accepted entries will be listed in the new Hermes Marketplace.

First place is $10,000; submissions are due 5pm EST on Nov 11 via a catalog pull request, a demo video tagging @NousResearch, and a Typeform. Judges score usefulness, reliability, polish, and creativity, and favor plugins that do more than a prompt or skill could.

item.title: Nous unifies Hermes plugins, connectors, and skills in a single Hermes Marketplace
item.description:
Nous Research announced on Nov 4 (11:11am PT) that plugins, connectors, and skills for Hermes Agent are now unified in one Hermes Marketplace, so you can browse and extend Hermes in a few clicks.

The marketplace page describes browsing skills and plugins plus hosted connectors for the apps you already use. The post passed about 72,000 views within hours.

item.title: OpenAI officially adds GPT-6.1 Terra to the models that power dots
item.description:
OpenAI added an update dated Nov 3 to its dots launch post: "We're expanding the family of frontier models that power dots to include GPT‑6.1 Terra." It says a dot "can draw on different models for different parts of its work," and that Terra builds on the GPT‑6 series' alignment work and uses safeguards developed for GPT‑6 Astra.

This makes official what dots lead Tibo (@thsottiaux) previewed on Nov 2, when he said Terra brings speed and a personality upgrade and will help bring dots to more people.

OpenAI has not announced any change to who can get dots. The help center still lists Pro and Business Premium (Enterprise as an admin-enabled beta), and talk of dots coming to Plus is unconfirmed.

item.title: Hermes Agent v0.22.7 rolls up 174 PRs, including lead routing and cron jobs for Desktop Group Chats
item.description:
Nous Research released Hermes Agent v0.22.7 on Nov 3 (about 1:53pm PT), one day after v0.22.6. It is a patch release that rolls up about 174 merged PRs for the CLI, installers, the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud, with full curated notes again deferred to v0.23.0.

Listed additions include opt-in lead routing for Desktop Group Chats (with a Lead badge), cron jobs that post into Group Chats, room purpose and shared notes, pinned Kanban boards as quick-switch tabs, TeX and mermaid diagram rendering, Telegram setup on Team Gateway by linking an account to the shared bot, an opt-in Slack setting to stay quiet on unaddressed thread replies, and a "Daybreak" switch for catalog-listed ChatGPT subscription models.

Teknium recommended upgrading for multi-machine and gateway users.

item.title: Nous opens a waitlist for the Hermes Agent mobile app after the beta filled up
item.description:
Nous Research said on Nov 3 (11:12am PT) that the Hermes Mobile beta it released at NousCon 2026 "filled up quickly," and that it is working to free up more beta seats and get the app production-ready for a wider release.

In the meantime, people can join the waitlist at hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/mobile. Teknium added that waitlisted users will get in "as we get more seats." No public release date was given.

item.title: Meta's Muse can now dance: share an animated clip of your Muse to Instagram, Facebook or WhatsApp
item.description:
Alexandr Wang posted a "Muse feature alert" on Nov 3 (12:55pm PT): you can now make your Muse dance. In your Muse chat, tap your Muse, hit the share button at the top right, and share the dancing clip to Instagram, Facebook or WhatsApp, or save it.

He added that if your Muse is connected to Instagram you can post straight from Instagram's add-story screen by picking your Muse. He spent the afternoon reposting user clips, and the feature post passed about 47,000 views within a few hours.

It is a fun, social feature rather than a new agent capability. Separately, Wang is still teasing "early access to phone calling" for Muse in a sash-patch guessing game, which Meta has not officially announced.

item.title: Hermes Agent v0.22.6 ships a migration command for Grok Bot users, and Nous pitches it at Musk's cost comment
item.description:
Nous Research released Hermes Agent v0.22.6 on Nov 2, a patch release that rolls up about 776 merged PRs since v0.22.5 for the CLI, installers, the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes are promised with v0.23.0.

The listed additions include hermes migrate and setup steps that move Grok Bot and OpenBot users over, a web app served from the gateway (hermes webapp), /model reset, per-skill locks against autonomous edits, hermes cron cancel with a missed-run policy, opt-in OS keychain storage for the vault key, and a pre_llm_call hook that can block a turn before inference.

The same day, the official @NousResearch account posted just "> hermes migrate grok-bot" quoting Elon Musk's remark that Grok Bot's serving cost was "unsustainably high relative to revenue" (about 87k views by evening). Teknium also hinted that more is "coming this thursdee."

item.title: OpenAI's dots lead says GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Terra will power dots, to bring dots to more people
item.description:
Tibo (@thsottiaux), who leads dots at OpenAI, posted on Nov 2 (7:50am PT) that OpenAI is "working on expanding the family of frontier models that power dots, including GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Terra and some others in the future." He said Terra "brings speed and a nice personality upgrade, and will help us bring dots to more people."

In a follow-up he added that "your dot will choose the best model for the task, drawing on different models for different parts of the work." The post passed 1 million views.

This is a plan, not a shipped change: OpenAI hasn't said when it lands or which plans get it. Some X coverage reads "more people" as dots coming to Plus, but that is unconfirmed. Dots still require Pro or Business Premium per the help center.

item.title: Grok Bot's GitHub and other source control integrations broke for 75 minutes early Monday
item.description:
The SpaceXSI status page reported "Issues with source control integrations" affecting Grok Bot and the Cursor desktop IDE from 1:09am to 2:24am PT on Monday, Nov 2.

During that window, source control provider integrations didn't work in either product, so bots that work with repositories could fail. The incident is marked resolved, and an outages.live record puts it at 1 hour 15 minutes.

item.title: Amazon's Jassy says outside shopping agents like Muse are "not great" yet, and bets on Alexa for Shopping instead
item.description:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy told analysts on the Q3 earnings call that few customers shop through outside AI agents yet because "the experience is still not great," and that Amazon's own Alexa for Shopping will be "the primary shopping agent customers use to shop Amazon." He didn't name Muse, which Amazon has blocked since September.

Amazon says more than 400 million customers used Alexa for Shopping in the past year and that US users spend 50% more per order. Meta, meanwhile, says shopping is the top use of Muse, with Shopify, Walmart and Best Buy signed on as partners.

A CNBC analysis on Nov 1 cites an audit of 51 large US retailers that found only five, including Amazon, explicitly restrict AI agents, while 37 block them mostly by accident through old anti-scraper rules.

item.title: DeepSeek open-sources dsh-superagent, a research prototype of an always-on agent that takes work from GitHub and chat
item.description:
DeepSeek's Harness team published dsh-superagent on GitHub on Oct 31 under the MIT license. It is a proactive coding agent for one repository that listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu, opens a work item when an allowed person asks, works in its own session and directory, and replies with results such as a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

The README says it is a research prototype, "not an official DeepSeek product," and not the same as DeepSeek's internal version. It runs on your own machine through DeepSeek Harness and needs a dedicated GitHub account for the agent, per its deployment guide.

Posts on X are pitching it as an open-source challenger to Grok Bot, Muse, dots and Claude Duet, but for now it is a team coding agent, not a consumer personal agent. It passed about 4,100 stars within a day.

item.title: Musk says Grok Bot cost "unsustainably high" relative to revenue, signaling usage limits were tightened on purpose
item.description:
Asked on X whether Grok Bot users would get a usage reset after many said their allowance ran out unusually fast this week, Elon Musk replied that "the cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue" (12:34pm PT, Nov 1).

That reads as confirmation that the overnight jump in usage meters was a deliberate tightening of Grok Bot limits for cost reasons, not just a dashboard glitch, and that no reset is coming. It contrasts with earlier statements that real metering was unaffected by the Oct 31 to Nov 1 billing and usage dashboard incident.

xAI hasn't published new limit numbers or an official announcement yet, so the exact size of the change is unknown.

item.title: Grok Bot and Cloud Agents were degraded for about 45 minutes late Friday night
item.description:
The SpaceXAI status page logged a "Multiple services degraded" incident that hit Grok Bot, Cloud Agents, Automations and cursor.com from 11:04pm to 11:47pm PT on Friday, Oct 30.

It was rated a minor disruption and is now resolved. The status page posted only "investigating" and "resolved" updates, with no cause given.

item.title: Grok Bot engineer Lauren (poteto) shares her bot-building guide and her "dr eggbot" bot designer
item.description:
Lauren (@poteto), who works on Grok Bot at SpaceXSI, posted a short guide on Saturday to building good Bots and managing a Bot team. It passed 400,000 views and 10,000 bookmarks, and the official @bot account is now replying to hundreds of people who ask it to send the guide to their own Bot.

Her main tips:

  • Add her dr eggbot template, a Bot that designs other Bots.
  • A few good Bots beat a big team.
  • Have Bots write skills for themselves as you teach them tasks, and optionally keep those skills in a private GitHub repo.
  • Give Bots connectors, the Vault, and their own email address so they can sign up for accounts on their own.
  • Brain-dump in voice mode, then ask the Bot to "restate this in your own words."

Later she teased something "really fun" coming "some time tomorrow," quoting her Oct 28 post about buying a new domain. She didn't say what it is.

item.title: Muse now shows up in the iPhone Share sheet, so you can send photos, links and files straight to your chat
item.description:
The official Muse account announced on Friday that you can tap Share in any iOS app to send photos, links and files directly into your Muse chat.

This lets you hand your agent material from Safari, Photos or Files without copying and pasting. The post only mentions iOS, and there was no word on Android.

item.title: Alexandr Wang nods to Muse's real-time voice mode, which has been quietly reaching users since Oct 24
item.description:
Meta's Alexandr Wang quoted a user's post on Saturday with just "👀🗣️👂". The user, Bill Doty, wrote that "muse voice is soooo good" and that it "quietly rolled out on 10/24 apparently."

Meta showed live voice conversations with Muse at Connect on Sept 23, with Muse working in the background while you talk. All Things Muse, citing TestingCatalog and user reports, says the feature started appearing for some users on Oct 24, with a "Give your Muse a voice" setup screen.

Meta still hasn't formally announced the rollout or said who is eligible. Wang's post is the closest thing to an official nod so far.

item.title: OpenAI's dots help page now says you can create a dot from the ChatGPT mobile app
item.description:
OpenAI updated its Getting started with your dot help article on Oct 30. It now says you can create a dot in the ChatGPT mobile app on iOS or Android, as well as in the desktop app or on desktop web, as long as you have the latest mobile app.

At launch, the release notes said dots had to be created on desktop, and the mobile app was only for talking to one afterward. The article also says the desktop app now works on Windows, and that dots still don't work on mobile web.

OpenAI hasn't posted a release note about mobile setup, so this change is only in the help center.

item.title: OpenAI confirms ChatGPT and Codex will share one token-based usage allowance starting in December
item.description:
A new OpenAI help article, Understanding ChatGPT and Codex usage limits, updated on Saturday, confirms something that had only been rumored on X. Starting in December, Plus, Pro and Business plans will have one usage allowance shared across ChatGPT and Codex, as OpenAI brings Work's agent features into the main ChatGPT experience.

  • Usage will be measured in tokens, so bigger models and harder tasks use more of it.
  • Instant chat won't count against the allowance.
  • Your combined remaining usage and reset times will show in Settings, under Usage. When you run out, you can wait, upgrade, or buy credits.

The article doesn't mention dots. But according to the dots help page, Codex and Work tasks a dot starts already count toward your plan limits. OpenAI still hasn't published permanent usage terms for dots themselves.

item.title: Nous opens the Hermes Agent mobile app beta to everyone on iPhone and Android
item.description:
Nous Research now has a public Hermes Mobile Beta sign-up page where anyone can reserve a spot in the official Hermes Agent app, through TestFlight on iPhone or Firebase App Distribution on Android. Last week a Nous co-founder only confirmed the beta existed, and on Friday it was handed to NousCon attendees.

According to early testers on X, the app lets you chat with your agent and watch its tool calls, talk to it hands-free in a Live mode, run routines that deliver to Telegram, Discord, Slack or Teams, install skills, track usage and spend, and open a terminal over SSH. You can sign in with Nous or connect your own self-hosted Hermes. Spots are limited, and some Android testers report hitting a tester cap. The latest tagged Hermes release is still v0.22.5.

item.title: NVIDIA's NemoClaw blueprints now officially support Hermes Agent, letting teams run it in a locked-down sandbox on their own hardware
item.description:
NVIDIA's Oct 30 technical blog post says its open-source NemoClaw blueprints currently support three agent harnesses: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent from Nous Research, and LangChain Deep Agents. A blueprint wraps the agent with Nemotron open models, NeMo optimization tools, and NVIDIA's OpenShell runtime, which controls what the agent can touch in files, networks, credentials, and tools.

There's a dedicated NemoClaw for Hermes Agent blueprint page, and the Hermes quickstart sets it up with one installer command (NEMOCLAW_AGENT=hermes) or nemohermes onboard. NVIDIA says it blocks outbound network access by default and runs locally, in the cloud, on DGX Spark, or on RTX PCs.

item.title: OpenAI dots had elevated search errors for about 1.5 hours on Friday afternoon
item.description:
OpenAI's status page logged elevated errors with search in dots, ChatGPT Work, and some ChatGPT thinking experiences on Friday, Oct 30. OpenAI started investigating at 12:38pm PT and marked it resolved at 2:14pm PT.

OpenAI rated it a minor incident and didn't give a cause.

item.title: Alexandr Wang calls a user’s Muse insurance switch "personal superintelligence"
item.description:
Meta's Alexandr Wang posted on Friday: "if this isn't personal superintelligence i don't know what is." The post drew about 186,000 views.

He was quoting a user, @MistrDeplorable, who says Muse moved him from a $2,123 GEICO renewal to a $1,536 Progressive policy with better coverage, then phoned GEICO to cancel and merged him into the call when GEICO asked to speak with him. Those savings figures are the user's own claim and haven't been independently checked.

Wang has been promoting user stories like this one since saying Muse "can make you $1,000." A separate viral story this week, about a user who says Muse filed a small-claims case that ended in a refund, is also circulating on X.

item.title: OpenAI keeps extended dots limits for now, separate from your plan usage, as it doubles Pro and Business Premium limits
item.description:
OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux said on Thursday that OpenAI will "continue offering extended limits for dots for now," and that dot usage will stay separate from your default ChatGPT usage. Dots launched with extended limits for the first month only, so the permanent per-plan dots terms people expected around today still haven't been published.

In the same post, OpenAI doubled all usage limits for the Pro 100, 200 and 500 tiers and Business Premium, effective immediately, and dropped the planned cut to Pro 200's Work and Codex allowance. Andrew Ambrosino added that OpenAI started a sprint to make the app simpler and faster. BleepingComputer notes OpenAI still gives no exact numbers per tier.

The dots help page still says Pro access excludes the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, and that prices for extra dots or more speed are coming later.

item.title: SpaceXSI launches Grok for Startups: one credit balance across Grok, Grok Build, Grok Bot and the Grok API
item.description:
SpaceXSI has a new Grok for Startups program. It gives startups credits that work across Grok, Grok Build, Grok Bot and the Grok API from one balance, plus hands-on onboarding.

  • Credits are sized to your stage, and SpaceXSI says it aims for "six to twelve months of real usage." No dollar amount is published.
  • You get 20% when you're approved, and the other 80% is released once you're up and running.
  • To qualify you need venture backing, a live product, and a company email that matches your website. You apply here with an xAI team ID.

The page went up around Oct 25, and posts about it spread widely on X on Thursday.

item.title: Similarweb: Grok Bot daily users grew 16 days in a row, and Musk points out it has no free tier
item.description:
Similarweb posted that as of October 26, Grok Bot's daily active users had grown for 16 days in a row, its longest growth streak so far.

Elon Musk quoted a post about the chart and added that Grok Bot "has no free tier." That post, from @XFreeze, reads the chart as going from under 100,000 daily users in early September to over 600,000 by October 26. That figure is a fan's reading of the chart, not a number Similarweb or SpaceXSI stated.

item.title: Grok Bot's Auto-review is degraded Thursday afternoon, according to the status page
item.description:
The status page opened a minor incident, "Auto Review Degradation," at 4:44pm PT on Thursday. It marks the Grok Bot component as degraded and says the team is investigating.

A separate minor "Cloud Agent Degradation" incident opened at 4:29pm PT affects Cloud Agents, Automations and the IDE, not Grok Bot. As of about 5:15pm PT, both were still under investigation and neither had a fix posted.

item.title: Globe and Mail: Canada's big banks block AI agents like Muse, which is still Canada's most popular app
item.description:
The Globe and Mail reports that a month after launch, Meta's Muse is still the most popular app in Canada. Businesses are now deciding how much access to give it and other agents.

  • Royal Bank of Canada said this week it is blocking third-party agents from its digital properties, including online banking. Bank of Montreal and TD have also blocked them.
  • Scotiabank is limiting agents, and CIBC says it doesn't support agents opening or accessing accounts. Wealthsimple and Neo are more open to them.
  • Shopify has integrated with Muse so people can buy from Shopify stores through it. The paper's own test purchase took 30 minutes and failed several times before it worked.

item.title: Grok Bot 0.78.1 adds shopping cards with order tracking, and templates that cancel trials and unused subscriptions
item.description:
The Grok Bot changelog lists v0.78.1 (Oct 27, also covering 0.78.0). Shopping with a Bot now shows products as cards with photos, rating, price and store, three or four results scroll in a carousel, and Buy now starts an order you approve. After an order, the Bot tracks it and tells you when it ships or arrives.

New templates include Try it, don't pay for it (starts a free trial and cancels it or reminds you before it bills), Find unused subscriptions and Watch subscription prices. Bots can now cancel a subscription or look up its renewal date, confirming with you first. Shop Pay can be connected in the Vault's Payments tab.

Other changes: Bots can start cloud agents in a custom mode, the Bot's browser types one character at a time like a person, and Team Bots get their own Vault logins and an Only you sharing option.

item.title: Grok Bot 0.77.0: a Permissions page in Settings, Import Memory from other assistants, and multi-question cards
item.description:
The Grok Bot changelog now lists v0.77.0 (Oct 26, also covering 0.76.0) as a full release. Settings gets a Permissions section that lists Auto-review rules under Always Ask and Allow without Asking, and Auto-review approval cards now stay open for 30 minutes instead of 10.

Import Memory brings your preferences and context from another AI assistant into your primary Bot. Bots can also ask several questions on one card that steps through them, chat tables get a copy button, and 1Password can connect without a shared vault, with you approving each login in 1Password.

The Vault and phone calls from this release window were covered earlier in this feed.

item.title: Meta's Muse launches in Singapore with Shopee, Grab, Singapore Airlines and other local connectors
item.description:
Meta announced that Muse is now available in Singapore on iOS, Android and muse.ai, with AI glasses support coming later. It is the next stop after the US and Canada launch in September and Japan on Oct 23; Alexandr Wang called it part of "muse's global tour."

Early local connector partners are Shopee, Grab, Singapore Airlines, Agoda, ShopBack, Klook, Trip.com and Lazada, rolling out progressively, alongside Gmail, Google Calendar and Instagram. Meta says Muse is free for most uses with paid plans for more; The Straits Times reports a weekly free usage limit and plans from S$22 to S$139.

In its hands-on, The Straits Times found Muse booked a restaurant table easily but failed to cancel it, and once suggested a restaurant that had closed.

item.title: OpenAI dots can now use iCloud Mail and Calendar through ChatGPT's new plugins
item.description:
OpenAI added iCloud Mail and iCloud Calendar plugins to ChatGPT on Oct 27, on every plan across web, desktop and iOS. MacRumors and 9to5Mac confirm dots can use them too, so iCloud users can connect their Apple inbox and calendar to a dot for the first time, and a dot can even help set the plugins up.

Mail can search, read, draft and send iCloud email and look up contacts; Calendar can read, schedule and update events. Each plugin is connected separately with an Apple app-specific password, per OpenAI's help center.
